title_en: Purchase a $70 Nintendo eShop eGift Card From Newegg and Get a Bonus $10 eGift Card Alongside It for Free
summary_en: Newegg is offering a free $10 Nintendo eShop eGift Card as a purchase bonus for buying a $70 Nintendo eShop eGift Card, but it's only available while supplies last.
body_en:
If Nintendo's new Customer Appreciation Sale has you wishing for a little extra spending cash for the eShop, Newegg is here to help you out with a new gift card deal. For a limited time, the retailer is offering a free $10 Nintendo eShop eGift card to those who purchase a $70 Nintendo eShop gift card as a little bonus offer, though it won't be available for long ( see it here ).
The store page notes the offer is only available while supplies last, and there's no telling how much longer that will be, so you'll want to be quick to take advantage of it. If you decide to buy, it's also worth mentioning that both cards will be delivered to you via email for easy access, too.
With the holidays right around the corner, if you've been thinking about buying a Nintendo eShop gift card for someone you know - or maybe just as a treat for yourself - this offer is a nice way to check that off the to-do list and score $10 in bonus spending cash alongside. There's plenty you can put it towards right now as well, what with the Customer Appreciation Sale still going strong until September 26 .
As of the time of this writing, the sale is still full of discounts on everything from games to accessories to amiibo and more that you can put that extra money towards. If the former is on your mind, titles like Metroid Dread , Metroid Prime 4: Beyond , and Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2 are just a few deals we've spotted as part of the sale, but they just scratch the surface of what's available.
To see a big rundown of some of our favorite offers that have popped up so far, it's worth perusing our roundup of the best deals in Nintendo's Customer Appreciation Sale to see if anything else catches your eye.
Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.
